findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM).
findings.citation_text:
2-102.12(A) Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM). (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM.

The PIC could not provide verification of their CFPM certification during this inspection. The rules were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to have a CFPM available at all times of operation moving forward.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Multiple nozzles on the fountain drink machine were observed with accumulating soilage in the nozzle holes. The PIC was shown and stated that the nozzles were cleaned Monday (four days prior to the inspection) and that the observed brown stuff was soda. The same soilage was observed in the Mountain Dew and Lemonade nozzles. These nozzles need to be cleaned (wash/rinse/sanitize) more often, preferably daily or every other day to ensure that they do not accumulate filth and potentially contaminate people’s drinks. The nozzles were cleaned during the inspection to correct the immediate violation. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are maintained clean to sight/touch at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

The beef in the left most run of the right steam well in the front was observed with internal temperatures of 117F-119F. The PIC was shown and stated that the foods were placed into the unit approximately one hour prior to observation. The unit was turned up to provide for future safety concerns and the current batch of meat was discarded at the end of the shift (4 pm) to manage the immediate concern.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

1) The sani bucket near the registers was observed at approximately 10 ppm CL. 2) The sanitizer bay of the three part sink was observed with a CL concentration of approximately 10 ppm. The CL sanitizer utilized by the facility requires a concentration of 100-200 ppm free CL in solution to be effective. Education was conducted with staff and the PIC and the buckets remade to correct. Ensure that all sanitizers are maintained at effective concentration at all times in the solution.

findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The deflector for the ice machine has a small amount of pink slime build up observed during this inspection. The PIC was shown and cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the food contact surfaces are maintained clean and sanitized at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Milk containers observed in the front reach in cooler are observed open and partially empty without date marking. Per conversations with the PIC one of them was opened this morning and another was opened a couple days ago. Education was conducted. Once milk is opened/unsealed it required seven day date marking and to be used or discarded by the end of day seven. The PIC was notified and placed dates on the unsealed containers to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11 Floors, Walls, and Ceilings. Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

1) The ceiling tiles in the mixing room are of the acoustic type. Any kind of food preparation requires a smooth and easily cleanable surface for the ceiling tiles. Replace or coat with multiple layers of gloss paint. The PIC was shown and instructed to complete update prior to the next routine inspection. 
2) There are two large holes in the ceiling in the dry storage area that are in need of repair. Repair prior to the next routine inspection.
